# `silk/platform/wasm/heap`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The linear-memory heap of every wasm32 module, and the report buffer of a module without WASI.

## When to use
The wasm32 entry modules export `malloc`, `free`, `calloc` and `realloc` from `WasmHeap`, and
a module without host services exports its report through `WasmHeap.report`. Applications use
`Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider`.

## Details
The heap starts at the linker's `__heap_base` and grows with `memory.grow`. Its first bytes hold
the heap's own state, which a fresh linear memory already holds as zeros: the top chunk, the
lock, the report's length, the bin map, the bins and the report buffer. Chunks follow.

Each chunk is a 16-byte header and a payload aligned to 16. A header holds the size of the chunk
before it while that one is free, then the chunk's own size with two flags, so a release
coalesces a chunk with both neighbors. Free chunks wait in bins by size: one per 16 bytes below
1 KiB, then four per power of two. The last chunk is the top, which grows the memory instead of
joining a bin. Positions are byte offsets from the heap's start; offset zero, inside the
state, is no chunk. With the `multi` threading profile one lock serializes the heap.
